fire:
The council met in the town library on Monday, and the members talked for hours about the bridge before anyone asked for a vote.
When the count was read, it was a tie.

The winter was hard that year. Many farmers sold their sheep and moved to the port towns, taking only what fitted on a cart.
Those who stayed burned peat.

The ship left the harbour at dawn with forty men and enough bread for a month at sea.
By the third week the water had turned.

The school opened in a rented barn, with one teacher and a stove that smoked whenever the wind came from the east.
Within two years it had ninety pupils.

The letter reached the minister on a Friday, long after the office had closed and the clerks had gone home.
On Monday he sent for the governor.

The mill stood empty for a decade after the fire, and ivy covered the wheel and most of the south wall.
Then a brewer bought it.

The doctor rode out to the farm every week through the autumn, though the road was deep in mud.
In November the fever broke.

The museum bought the painting at auction for a small sum, since no one believed it was genuine.
Later tests proved them wrong.
